title: Raw sprout food-safety boundaries
summary: Sprouting seed in warm humid conditions can also support harmful bacteria; raw sprouts are not a risk-free emergency crop.
steps: Use seed sold for edible sprouting from a trustworthy source, not treated garden seed.
Sanitise hands, containers and work surfaces and use safe water throughout.
Keep batches separate, dated and small enough to inspect; discard any batch with abnormal odour, slime, mould or poor drainage.
Refrigerate finished sprouts promptly and prevent contact with raw meat, dirty produce or contaminated water.
For people at higher risk of foodborne illness, choose thoroughly cooked sprouts or another cooked crop instead of raw sprouts.
warnings: Rinsing cannot guarantee removal of pathogens that may be inside sprout tissue.
Never eat garden seed labelled as treated, coated or not for food use.
common_mistakes: Scaling up before a small controlled trial.
